title: Kepler's laws
examples: How do Kepler's laws help us predict planet positions?
What is the difference between a circle and an ellipse in orbits?
Can you explain the relationship between the period and the distance using the laws?

explain.say: Kepler first described how planets move around the Sun.
The first law states that planets orbit the Sun in an ellipse.
Kepler's second law says a line connecting planet and Sun sweeps equal areas in equal times.
The third law relates the period squared to the cube of the average distance.
In our solar system, planets follow these three important rules for their paths.
Think about the Moon orbiting the Earth; its path is also an ellipse.

faq.q: Does the planet's mass affect Kepler's laws?
faq.a: No, Kepler's laws describe the motion around a central body. The mass of the orbiting planet does not change these relationships.
asks: Is the planet's mass included in the calculation?

faq.q: What does 'perihelion' mean in simple terms?
faq.a: Perihelion is the point in the orbit where the planet is closest to the Sun. At this point, the planet moves fastest.
asks: Where is the planet closest to the Sun?
What is the nearest point in the orbit?

faq.q: If I double the distance, what happens to the period?
faq.a: According to the third law, the period squared would increase by a factor of eight. This means the period increases by a factor of two.
asks: How does T relate to r if r doubles?
If r is multiplied by two, what is T multiplied by?

faq.a: No, most orbits are ellipses. A circle is just a special case of an ellipse where the two foci are at the same point.
asks: Can an orbit look like a circle?

faq.q: Why is the area sweeping rate constant?
faq.a: This constant rate is due to the conservation of angular momentum. It means the product of the distance and the speed is always the same.
asks: What physical principle keeps the area sweeping constant?

facts: Orbits are generally elliptical, not circular.
The fastest speed occurs at perihelion.
The relationship is T squared is proportional to r cubed.
The law of equal areas is a consequence of conservation of angular momentum.

quiz.say: If a planet's average orbital distance increases by a factor of four, how does its period change?
quiz.why: Because T squared is proportional to r cubed, if r is multiplied by four, T squared is multiplied by four cubed, which is sixty-four. The period T is the square root of sixty-four, which is eight.

wrong.0: This confuses the relationship by assuming T is proportional to r squared.
wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes T is only proportional to r.
wrong.2: This treats the relationship as linear, ignoring the cubic relationship.

quiz.say: Which shape best describes a planet's orbit around a star?
quiz.why: Kepler's first law specifically states that planetary orbits are ellipses, which are oval shapes.

wrong.1: While a circle is an ellipse, it is not the general rule for all orbits.
wrong.2: A parabola describes objects that escape the gravitational pull entirely.
wrong.3: A hyperbola describes an object that passes by but does not orbit.

quiz.say: When is a planet moving fastest in its orbit?
quiz.why: The law of equal areas dictates that the planet moves fastest when it is closest to the central body, which is perihelion.

wrong.0: Speed is constantly changing unless the orbit is perfectly circular.
wrong.2: At aphelion, the planet is farthest away and therefore moves the slowest.
wrong.3: The speed is related to the time taken, not just the size of the area.
